passages.title: Love supplies the aim against teaching that produces empty disputes
passages.summary: The letter is addressed from Paul to Timothy, his true child in faith. Timothy is to stay in Ephesus and stop certain people from teaching different doctrine. They occupy themselves with myths and endless lists of ancestors. The law is good when used lawfully, against the lawless. Paul thanks Christ, who put him in service though he was a persecutor. Christ Jesus came to save sinners, and Paul calls himself the chief. Timothy is to fight the good fight with faith and a good conscience. Hymenaeus and Alexander have wrecked their faith.
passages.uncertainty: The marker identifies Ephesus. No exact meeting house or journey through Macedonia is assigned.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson teaches sound doctrine as protection against false instruction. Why does the aim of love require both sound teaching and a good conscience?

contextNote.title: Love supplies the aim against teaching that produces empty disputes
contextNote.text: Verse 3 tells Timothy to command certain people to stop. Verse 4 says their teaching produces disputes and not God’s work in faith. Verse 5 gives the goal of the command, and it is love. That love has three sources: a pure heart, a good conscience, and sincere faith. Verse 6 says some have missed these and turned to empty talk. So the test of teaching here is what it produces. Verse 19 repeats two of the three: faith and a good conscience.

passages.title: Prayer for everyone leads into instructions shaped by unequal roles
passages.summary: Paul urges prayer for all people, and for kings and all in authority. The aim is a quiet and peaceful life. God wants all people to be saved and to know the truth. There is one God and one mediator, who gave himself for all. Men are to pray without anger. Women are to dress modestly and adorn themselves with good works. The letter says a woman should learn quietly and not teach a man. It gives Adam and Eve as its reason.
passages.uncertainty: The marker identifies Ephesus. No exact meeting house or journey through Macedonia is assigned.

lds.text: How does the claim about one mediator support prayer for everyone?

contextNote.title: Prayer for everyone leads into instructions shaped by unequal roles
contextNote.text: Verse 1 asks prayer “for all men,” and verse 2 names kings. Verse 4 gives the reason: God desires all people to be saved. Verse 5 supports that with two “ones.” There is one God, so no people has a different one. There is one mediator between God and humans, the man Christ Jesus. Verse 6 completes it: he gave himself as a ransom for all. One God and one mediator for all is why prayer covers all.

passages.title: Care for a household becomes a test of care for the assembly
passages.summary: The letter gives the qualities of an overseer. He must be without reproach, the husband of one wife, and able to teach. He must not be a drinker, violent, or a lover of money. He must rule his own house well and not be a new convert. Servants of the assembly must also be tested first. Their wives must be reverent and faithful. Paul writes so Timothy will know how to behave in God’s house. The chapter ends with a short confession about Christ revealed in the flesh.
passages.uncertainty: The marker identifies Ephesus. No exact meeting house or journey through Macedonia is assigned.

lds.text: Why does care for a household supply a test for care of the assembly?

contextNote.title: Care for a household becomes a test of care for the assembly
contextNote.text: Verse 4 requires an overseer to rule his own house well. Verse 5 gives the reason as a question in brackets. One who cannot rule his own house cannot care for God’s assembly. The comparison rests on a picture stated in verse 15. The assembly is called the house of God. So the smaller house shows how he will act in the larger one. The verbs differ: “rule” for the house, “take care of” for the assembly.

passages.title: Received gifts and visible conduct answer restrictions and contempt for youth
passages.summary: The Spirit says that in later times some will leave the faith. They will forbid marriage and command people to abstain from foods. The letter answers that God created foods to be received with thanks. Everything God made is good. Timothy is to teach this and avoid profane fables. Bodily exercise has some value, but godliness has value for all things. No one should despise his youth. He is to attend to reading, exhortation, and teaching, and use his gift.
passages.uncertainty: The marker identifies Ephesus. No exact meeting house or journey through Macedonia is assigned.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson teaches becoming a faithful example despite youth. Why must Timothy's visible conduct support the instruction he gives?

contextNote.title: Received gifts and visible conduct answer restrictions and contempt for youth
contextNote.text: Verse 3 names two rules of these teachers: no marriage and certain foods forbidden. Verse 4 answers with creation. Every creature of God is good. Nothing is to be rejected if it is received with thanksgiving. The condition matters: the food is received as a gift. Verse 5 says it is made holy by God’s word and prayer. Verse 3 already said God created these foods to be received.

passages.title: Family duties and tested testimony shape care and correction
passages.summary: Timothy is to treat older men as fathers and older women as mothers. The assembly should honor widows who are truly alone. A widow with children or grandchildren should be cared for by them. A widow is enrolled only if she is sixty and known for good works. Younger widows should marry. Elders who rule well deserve double honor, for the worker deserves his wages. An accusation against an elder needs two or three witnesses. Timothy is told to use a little wine for his stomach.
passages.uncertainty: The marker identifies Ephesus. No exact meeting house or journey through Macedonia is assigned.

lds.text: How do family duties and tested testimony limit careless decisions about support?

contextNote.title: Family duties and tested testimony shape care and correction
contextNote.text: Verse 3 says to honor widows “who are widows indeed.” Verse 4 puts the first duty on children and grandchildren. Caring for a parent is called piety and repayment. It is “acceptable in the sight of God.” Verse 8 says one who will not provide has denied the faith. Verse 16 gives the purpose: the assembly can then relieve widows who are alone.

passages.title: Contentment and generous use answer the pursuit of wealth as religious gain
passages.summary: Servants are told to honor their masters so that God’s name is not blasphemed. The letter warns against teachers who think godliness is a way to gain. Godliness with contentment is great gain. We brought nothing into the world and can carry nothing out. The love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. Timothy is to flee these things and fight the good fight of faith. The rich are told not to be proud or to trust in uncertain riches. Timothy is to guard what was entrusted to him.
passages.uncertainty: The marker identifies Ephesus. No exact meeting house or journey through Macedonia is assigned.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson teaches sound doctrine as protection against false instruction. How does generous sharing answer the temptation to treat faith as private gain?

contextNote.title: Contentment and generous use answer the pursuit of wealth as religious gain
contextNote.text: Verses 9–10 warn those who want to be rich. Verse 17 then speaks to those who already are. It tells them where not to put hope: in uncertain riches. Verse 18 says what to do with wealth, in four phrases. Do good, be rich in good works, be ready to give, be willing to share. The word “rich” is turned: the wealth that counts is good works. Verse 19 calls this a good foundation for the time to come.

words.label: Gentiles
words.meaning: People of nations other than Israel.

words.label: Apostles
words.meaning: People sent out with a message. In the Gospels the word names twelve whom Jesus chose.

words.label: Saints
words.meaning: People set apart as holy. In the letters the word means the believers in a place.

words.label: Assembly
words.meaning: A gathering of people. In the New Testament letters it means a group of believers. Many translations say “church.”
